The aicr-gate image now ships only the statically linked Go gate binary built from this module's pins, so a future finding on it must be fixed by a dependency bump, not re-suppressed. Confirmation is the first Weekly Image Vulnerability Scan run after merge: aicr-gate must report 0 HIGH+ and 0 VEX-suppressed. v13 added aiperf-bench GHSA-cq5v-8q36-5273 (aiohttp 3.13.5 C-parser out-of-bounds read) and is the first statement in this document justified vulnerable_code_cannot_be_controlled_by_adversary rather than vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path: the compiled C parser does parse every benchmark response, so the claim rests on every aiohttp peer being a cluster-internal workload discovered through the Kubernetes API. The v13 stale audit re-scanned ghcr.io/nvidia/aicr-validators/aiperf-bench:scan-90ef73c8 with the pinned grype 0.110.0 and found all 34 pre-existing statements still applied (declared and applied sets identical, zero stale). aiperf-bench is now the only product in this document, so no other image needs auditing. v14 has two halves. First, it added seven aiperf-bench statements for the openssl 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 HIGH findings the 2026-08-27 scan reported on libssl3t64 and openssl-provider-fips (CVE-2026-14456, CVE-2026-14457, CVE-2026-18798, CVE-2026-54874, CVE-2026-63072, CVE-2026-63075, CVE-2026-63076: 7 CVEs x 2 packages = the 14 rows). Diffing full grype runs of the two bases shows the bump clears 32 findings including 7 HIGH and introduces no new HIGH; the only two rows that move forward are CVE-2026-72522 (libexpat1) and CVE-2025-15367 (CPython), both Medium and both already present on the older versions, so neither is newly suppressed. vulnerability.name: GHSA-cq5v-8q36-5273
vulnerability.description: aiohttp: out-of-bounds heap read in the C HTTP parser while building the error message for a malformed response, which an attacker-controlled server (or an accidentally malformed response) can turn into a client-side DoS (CVE-2026-69244, CWE-125, High CVSS 7.1). Present via aiohttp 3.13.5. Fixed only in aiohttp 3.14.3, which no bump can reach: aiperf pins `aiohttp~=3.13.3` (>=3.13.3,<3.14) in pyproject.toml at both v0.11.0 (the version installed here) and v0.12.0 (newest upstream release, 2026-08-06), so requiring 3.14.3 in validators/performance/requirements.txt would make pip resolution fail outright rather than produce a fixed image. Unlike the other statements in this document the vulnerable code IS on the execute path -- aiohttp is the benchmark's request transport -- so the claim rests on adversary control of the response bytes, not on unreachability.

statements.impact_statement: The defect is in HttpParser.feed_data's error path at aiohttp/_http_parser.pyx:588-590 of 3.13.5: `after = cparser.llhttp_get_error_pos(self._cparser)` yields a raw `const char*` into the fed buffer, and the following `after.split(b"\r\n", 1)` forces an implicit char*-to-bytes conversion whose strlen() scans past the end of that buffer looking for a NUL. aio-libs/aiohttp PR #13222 (commit 49f65d5, released in 3.14.3) fixes it by slicing the snippet out of the bounded `data` object instead. This code is genuinely live in the image -- the compiled parser ships at /opt/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/aiohttp/_http_parser.cpython-313-x86_64-linux-gnu.so and the image config sets no AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS (verified with `crane config`), so the C parser, not the unaffected Python one, parses every benchmark response. What makes the image not_affected is that the parser only enters this branch when a peer emits a malformed HTTP message, and no peer aiperf-bench talks to is attacker-influenced. The installed aiperf 0.11.0 constructs exactly four aiohttp.ClientSession objects. (1) transports/aiohttp_client.py:139 is the benchmark request transport, shared by common/readiness_probe.py; its only target is the --url value, which buildAIPerfJob (validators/performance/inference_perf_constraint.go:2964) fills from resolveInferenceEndpoint -- a cluster-internal Service URL of the form http://<svc>.<ns>.svc:<port> discovered through the Kubernetes API by resolveFrontendEndpoint/resolveGatewayEndpoint in the same file, pointing at the Dynamo frontend or inference gateway that this same validator deployed. No recipe, snapshot, CLI flag, or environment variable can redirect it; the file's only os.Getenv bindings cover timeouts, model, router mode, cache sizing, and image resolution. (2) and (3) common/mixins/base_metrics_collector_mixin.py:294 and :413 are the GPU-telemetry and server-metrics scrapers; GpuTelemetryConfig defaults the DCGM collector to a local exporter (http://localhost:9400/metrics) and ServerMetricsDiscoveryConfig defaults to mode=auto, which enumerates eligible in-cluster inference-server pods via the Kubernetes API -- both address only workloads inside the cluster under test. (4) dataset/dataset_manager.py:269 downloads media URLs carried in the dataset and is the one session that could reach an arbitrary internet host; it is unreachable under AICR's fixed argv, which passes synthetic-prompt flags (--prompt-input-tokens-mean, --num-dataset-entries, --random-seed) with no --input-file and no public-dataset selector, so the dataset holds only generated text and the media-URL map stays empty. The same gating keeps dataset/loader/base_public_dataset.py, which fetches remote dataset archives over AioHttpClient, out of the run. Residual risk if a cluster-internal inference server were somehow made to emit malformed chunked framing is bounded: the flaw is an out-of-bounds read with no write primitive, and the process that would crash is a single-shot benchmark Job pod -- BackoffLimit 0, RestartPolicy Never, TTLSecondsAfterFinished 3600 in buildAIPerfJob -- running as non-root nvs (uid 1000) on a distroless base with no shell and no package manager. The outcome is a failed inference-perf validation, not a crossed security boundary.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-14456
vulnerability.description: openssl 3.5.6-1~deb13u2: unbounded resource consumption in the QUIC server listener. Per the OpenSSL advisory, "when an OpenSSL QUIC server (Listener SSL object) processes valid QUIC Initial packets for unknown destination connection IDs, it can allocate and queue new incoming channels without enforcing any limit". OpenSSL rates this LOW; Debian/NVD score it High, which is why grype surfaces it. Fixed in Debian at 3.5.7-1~deb13u2.

statements.impact_statement: The trigger requires the image to run an OpenSSL QUIC server, i.e. to create a Listener SSL object via SSL_new_listener on a context built with OSSL_QUIC_server_method and then accept QUIC Initial packets from peers. The aiperf-bench image runs no server of any kind: its entrypoint is the aiperf CLI acting purely as an HTTP client against an inference endpoint, and it listens on no port. OpenSSL's QUIC support is reached only through the dedicated QUIC API (OSSL_QUIC_client_method, OSSL_QUIC_server_method, SSL_new_listener and friends). Within the shipped image the only libssl/libcrypto consumers on the workload's path are CPython's _ssl.cpython-313-x86_64-linux-gnu.so and _hashlib.cpython-313-x86_64-linux-gnu.so, and CPython binds none of the affected subsystems: dir(ssl) and dir(_ssl) expose no symbol containing QUIC, DTLS, CMS or CMP, and the only protocol constants are PROTOCOL_SSLv23, PROTOCOL_TLS, PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT, PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER, PROTOCOL_TLSv1, PROTOCOL_TLSv1_1 and PROTOCOL_TLSv1_2. The 130-package Python closure installed from validators/performance/requirements.txt (aiperf==0.11.0) contains no QUIC or HTTP/3 implementation (no aioquic, no h3) and no binding to OpenSSL's CMS or CMP APIs (neither cryptography nor pyOpenSSL is present); the transports are aiohttp 3.13.5, httpx 0.28.1, requests 2.34.2 and urllib3 2.7.0, all HTTP over TCP. Nothing in the image can therefore construct a QUIC object, so the defect is unreachable. AICR runs the image only as `aiperf profile --model <text-LLM> --url <endpoint> --endpoint-type chat ...` from buildAIPerfJob in validators/performance/inference_perf_constraint.go, and every endpoint is a cluster-internal plain-HTTP Service URL of the form http://<svc>.<ns>.svc:<port> built by resolveFrontendEndpoint / resolveGatewayEndpoint (lines 2348, 2351, 2395 and 2399), so the benchmark path negotiates no TLS at all. There is also no command-line entry point into any OpenSSL subsystem: the `openssl` binary package is not installed (enumerating every path across all 48 base layers found no bin/openssl), and the distroless runtime ships no shell. The openssl-provider-fips rows are a source-version match on a module the process never maps. The image config sets OPENSSL_CONF=/etc/ssl/openssl-nofips.cnf, whose [provider_sect] activates default_sect only; there is no /etc/ssl/openssl.cnf and no /usr/lib/ssl (OPENSSLDIR is absent entirely), so /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/ossl-modules/fips.so is never loaded. Independently, the FIPS provider implements only cryptographic primitives (digests, ciphers, KDFs, DRBGs, signature algorithms); the QUIC and DTLS record layers live in libssl and the CMS and CMP implementations live in libcrypto, so none of this code is inside fips.so to begin with. Both flagged binary packages (libssl3t64 and openssl-provider-fips, both 3.5.6-1~deb13u2) enter only through the runtime base nvcr.io/nvidia/distroless/python:3.13-v4.1.1@sha256:6b49f6183eaec6dbd100219a43314bbf1d71b148eafcce62fdcc6472d066b5d9; scanning that base alone with the pinned grype 0.110.0 reproduces all 14 HIGH rows, so no AICR-authored layer contributes them, and syft places both packages in base layer sha256:72956fd1eb37d6802c3518bac58a3d138be3386834967797df1a3b851c0fc3db (/var/lib/dpkg/status.d/libssl3t64). No bump remediates: Debian fixes at 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, and v4.1.1 is already the newest NGC distroless python 3.13 tag. Every tag from the v4.0.8 this image shipped on before 2026-08-27 forward (v4.0.8, v4.0.9, v4.1.1) still carries 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 on a byte-identical openssl layer, the same layer digest quoted above, verified by scanning all three on 2026-08-27. So this is a VEX case rather than a base-image bump until NGC rebuilds on patched trixie.
